messages:
alex: Quick sync — considering an 'adaptive fanout' for internal API routing. Idea: route requests across pools based on tenant latency budget + model-cost score. Would let us trade cost for latency per-tenant. thoughts?

maria: love the idea in principle. question: how do we express budget in header/contract? tenant header or route claim?

alex: probably a header e.g., X-Tenant-Latency-Budget-ms and X-Tenant-Cost-Priority. runtime can map to pool weights.

sam: header seems brittle. can we derive from tenant profile in control plane? token exchange during auth could attach claims.

maria: +1 to deriving from control plane. also need telemetry hooks — per-route latency/cost breakdown so SRE can validate.

opsbot: deploy-bot: canary started for adaptive-fanout v1 on staging at 1712350000 :rocket: \n
jeff: concerning protobuf vs JSON: pools will host both gRPC (proto) and REST adapters. do we force proto internally for performance?

alex: prefer proto internally but need a gateway shim for browser clients. proposal: accept JSON at edge -> translate -> route proto between pools.

sam: translation adds CPU cost. maybe only translate for legacy clients, new clients register proto capability via client metadata.

maria: telemetry: instrument translation time and tokenization overhead separately. add labels: translation_ms, routing_decision, pool_id.

alex: quick config sketch:
```
policy:
  - if tenant.latency_budget < 200 -> route: low-latency-pool
  - else if tenant.cost_priority == "high" -> route: cost-optimized-pool
  - hints: client_proto_capable=true
```

jeff: action items?

alex: action items: 1) sam to prototype control-plane claim flow (due EOD Wed). 2) maria to draft telemetry labels + dashboard tiles. 3) jeff to list edge translation perf numbers.

jeff: noted. I'll post perf snapshot after lunch.

maria: small UX note — console should surface per-tenant effective SLO after routing rules apply, not just raw pool SLOs.

alex: agreed — makes it actionable for PMs. ok wrapping up, ping me if you need context. :thumbsup:
